To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the "owner computes/owner stores" rules for computation decomposition on DMPCs are not always the most appropriate, and (2) tiling on DMPCS must be performed in a way that is very different from the one that is used for SMPCs.

(1) data distribution and computation decomposition must be handled synergistically to obtain good performance on DMPCs and (2) the dominant data array must be identified in a program to allow the determination of data distribution and computation decompositions that minimize the overall execution cost on DMPCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do we determine a data decomposition for a given computation?
the design and implementation of a new approach to automatic data and computation decomposition for DMPCs.
the development of a systematic approach for handling computations and the distribution of the data in order to optimize the overall execution time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method is a very promising one for handling computations and distributed data on DMPCs in an integrated way, and that it has the potential to significantly improve the performance of many scientific programs.
, for a given application, the overall execution time is minimized when data decomposition and computation decomposition are determined simultaneously and when tiling is applied.

, in general, the overall method proposed in this article outperforms the other methods by a factor of two or more, and that the performance of the proposed method is very close to the performance of a perfect method that has complete information about the data and the computation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by combining computation and data decompositions, we were able to achieve better performance than the best known results for the heat equation and for Gaussian elimination with pivorting on DMPCs.

we have developed a new method for handling data and computation decomposition synergistically, which is based on a novel ranking of data, and on new algorithms for determining data decomposition and computation decomposition at the same time for each nested Do-Loop.
the overall method is able to handle efficiently the data and computation decomposition in a synergistic manner, which is crucial for DMPCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data distribution has a major effect on the overall execution time of a parallel program on DMPCs.
the decomposition of data and computation should be handled simultaneously, as opposed to the existing techniques that decompose the computation first and then determine a distribution of data.
the decomposition of data and computation on DMPCs should be performed synergistically, rather than sequentially, as is done in most existing methods.
